subject: Re: Demo follow-up — model fit, benchmarks & next steps
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@acmecommerce.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from today's demo — next steps & benchmarks request

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap from our side: Acme is focused on a hybrid retrieval + instruction pipeline for product search relevance (high throughput during peak hours) and a smaller set of high-quality generative responses for customer support. Two key asks we left the call with:

- Can you share Redwood-verified benchmark links for recommended models (throughput and latency percentiles)?
- Any recommended prompt sets / evals we should run to validate quality/regression?
- Estimated cost delta between a 7B quantized variant vs a 13B quantized variant for our expected QPS (peak ~120 TPS, sustained ~40 TPS).

Procurement timeline: we're targeting an internal decision by Aug 6, and procurement will need a high-level performance & cost summary to include in the SOW.

Would appreciate the links and a suggested next step (mutual action plan) — happy to sync again if useful.

Best,
Emily Chen
Head of AI Platforms
Acme Commerce
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@acmecommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — benchmarks request

Hi Emily —

Great talking earlier — thanks for the clear recap. Short answers up front and I attached a 1-pager (acme_benchmark_plan.pdf) with the mutual action plan.

Recommended models for your use-case:
- redwood-7b-q4f16: best cost/throughput for embedding + simple instruction tasks; good for high-QPS search rerank.
- redwood-13b-q4: higher quality for generative support responses and fewer hallucinations on long context.

Redwood-verified performance (from our internal suite, measured on A100 equivalent infra):
- redwood-7b-q4f16 @ seq=512: sustained throughput ~220 TPS (batching enabled), p50 latency 18 ms / p95 72 ms / p99 140 ms.
- redwood-13b-q4 @ seq=512: sustained throughput ~95 TPS, p50 latency 35 ms / p95 160 ms / p99 320 ms.

Cost delta (rough ballpark for Hosted API usage): 13b is ~2.5x the per-token cost vs the 7b quantized variant for comparable sequences. We'll add an itemized estimate in the attached 1-pager.

Suggested prompt sets / evals:
- Search rerank: 1k queries sampled from your production logs (we can share anonymized template).
- Support QA: 200 high-importance tickets + golden answers to run BLEU/ROUGE + human review on top 50.
- Regression checks: run monthly evals against a saved baseline prompt set and flag any >5% drop in top-K relevance or >10% drop in rated helpfulness.

Next steps (mutual action plan):
1) You share the sample prompt logs & success metrics (top-K precision for search, NPS or helpfulness for support).
2) We run a 2-week benchmark (hosted sandbox) with both model variants and provide TPS/latency/cost + qualitative examples.
3) Joint review + decision (we can support a short POC on Dedicated capacity if you want isolated throughput).

Attachments: acme_benchmark_plan.pdf (1-pager with timeline/costs).

Looping Marissa (solutions) to coordinate the sandbox and runbook. I can schedule a 30-min follow-up next week if helpful.

Cheers,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@acmecommerce.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 09:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — model fit, benchmarks & next steps

Thanks Alex — this is exactly the level of detail we need. A few clarifying questions before we share logs:

- For the regression thresholds you suggested, can you share an example alerting/action flow? We want to be sure our engineering team can integrate alerts with PagerDuty/Jira.
- For the 1k search queries: are there sample scripts you run client-side to anonymize PII before upload?
- Do you provide the prompt sets as JSONL? We prefer to run the evals in our staging environment first.

Procurement note: procurement asked for a DocuSign-ready SOW and an initial 30-day sandbox quote to evaluate peak TPS. Would you be able to provide that by July 29?

If it helps, we can schedule a 30-min sync Tue or Wed next week to walk through what we will upload.

Best,
Emily
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@acmecommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — model fit, benchmarks & next steps

Hi Emily —

Thanks — answers inline and next steps below.

- Regression alerting/action flow: we typically wire the eval harness into our monitoring pipeline. Example flow: monthly eval runs -> compare metrics to baseline -> if delta exceeds threshold, create Jira ticket with attached failing examples + open a PagerDuty incident for on-call ML infra if p99 latency or error-rate spikes. I attached a short runbook in the 1-pager and can share our Jira templates.

- PII anonymization: yes — we provide a small Python script that replaces email/SSN patterns and hashes user IDs before upload. We'll include that script in the Drive folder (link below).

- Prompt sets format: JSONL (one prompt per line) — I attached a starter prompts file (acme_model_fit_prompts.json) and uploaded the full set to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmeSharedBenchmarks. You can run locally in staging; we'll run the same suite inside the sandbox for apples-to-apples comparison.

DocuSign-ready SOW & 30-day sandbox quote: we'll have a draft SOW and sandbox pricing by Tue Jul 28 COB so you can circulate to procurement.

Quick technical notes (so your engineers have it up front):
- Sandbox environment will expose the same Redwood API surface with a sandbox key and limited-capacity Dedicated nodes.
- Benchmarks we will share (same as the verified profile): redwood-7b-q4f16 seq=512 (p50/p95/p99 numbers) and redwood-13b-q4 seq=512 — exact TPS depends on batching, KV cache hit rates, and request size.

Related links: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-2026-run1 (benchmark summary) | https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmeSharedBenchmarks (prompt sets & anonymization script) | HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-2026-07-01

Next actions:
- Emily: share the anonymized sample logs by Mon Jul 27 (or confirm if you want Redwood to run with a synthetic sample).
- Marissa: please schedule the sandbox kickoff and attach the runbook + Jira templates once ready.
- Alex: deliver draft SOW by Tue Jul 28.

Happy to jump on the Tue/ Wed sync — I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
